failures: Wiley Scholar Gateway free-tier quota exhausted (30/30, resets 2026-11-01): no classical reference could be confirmed in Wiley, so all pre-1946 items stay bibliographic_verified=false.

PubMed does not index the pre-1946 classical literature (Dexter 1902, Warren 1905/1911/1917, Reese 1910, Studnicka 1895/1905, Burckhardt 1894, Selenka 1891, Minot, Sorensen 1894, Hill 1894, Cameron, Dendy 1911, Melchers 1899, Sjovall 1909, Wallman 1858, Roofe 1934, Holmgren 1959 Breviora, Ariens-Kappers 1950 J Comp Neurol): lookup_article_by_citation returned NOT_FOUND for the ones tested.

WebSearch returns AI-written summaries, not page text: the 'excerpt' fields of web records are sentences quoted inside those summaries (themselves quoting OCR text of the UNSW Embryology wiki, Springer reference lists, Wiley/Zenodo/BHL listings) and must not be cited as direct quotation of the original papers.

Full reference lists of Dexter 1902, Warren 1905 and Warren 1917 could not be retrieved through WebSearch (only partial in-text citations); the UNSW Embryology transcriptions of these papers (embryology.med.unsw.edu.au, pages 'Paper - The development of the paraphysis in the common fowl (1903)' and '... in mammalia (1917)') should be opened by a human or a tool with page-fetch rights.

Original Francotte (human embryo, 12 weeks), D'Erchia (fish and mammal embryos), Herrick ('preparaphysis'), Osborn (amphibian brain plates), Ebbesson & Schroeder 1975 (Necturus paraphysis), Kappers 1955-57 compilations and Dandy 1921-22 (first successful removal of a paraphysial cyst) were mentioned only as in-text or second-hand citations; no title/volume was returned for them, so they were NOT recorded as separate records (see note on the Dexter and Warren records).

Gaupp's review on pineal, parietal organ and paraphysis (Ergebnisse der Anatomie und Entwicklungsgeschichte, c. 1904) is only a recollection offered by the search summary 'from memory'; no tool confirmed it, so it was not recorded.

Conflicting data between sources, left unresolved: Dexter paper year (1902 Wiley vs 1903 UNSW wiki); Sjovall year (1909 vs 1910); Warren 1917 page range (75-134 vs 75-135) and volume (28; one Springer list said 27); Cameron pineal paper year (1902-05); Reese year (1910 repository vs 1922 catalogue); Ariens-Kappers 1950 last page (127 vs 128). One search summary wrongly attributed the 1917 mammalian paraphysis paper to Percival Bailey; all other results (Zenodo DOI 10.1002/cne.900280103, UNSW wiki, Harvard affiliation) point to John Warren, and Bailey 1916 papers concern the roof plate / choroid plexus only.
Direct HTTP to blocked domains was not attempted; archive.org, BHL, Zenodo and UNSW pages were only reachable as WebSearch hits, not fetched.

records.title: On the pineal area and adjacent structures of the brain of the dipnoan fish, Protopterus annectens (Owen)
records.query: Holmgren 1959 "On the pineal area and adjacent structures of the brain of the dipnoan fish, Protopterus annectens (Owen)" Breviora
records.excerpt: Burckhardt's 1890 and 1892 publications offered a short account of the brain's dorsal region. They noted a pineal organ and a prominent inner structure that Burckhardt called the "coronarium."
records.note: Key source for the old lungfish term 'coronarium' (Burckhardt 1890, 1892). A Protopterus study at the same archive.org file (biostor-283290) judges the structure in front of the velum transversum a true paraphysis cerebri, following Studnicka 1905 and Kappers 1956-57, and states that the paraphysis belongs morphologically to the telencephalon. Five specimens, Bouin or formol-alcohol, celloidin and paraffin sections. Breviora no. 109, May 1959 (Museum of Comparative Zoology).
